import { Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'
import client from '../../../../snippets/client.ts?raw'
import react from '../../../../snippets/react.tsx?raw'

`@familiar-ai/client` connects to the HTTP API, mirrors what its event streams send and derives the transcript a chat UI renders for a room. Familiar's own web app is built on it.

```sh
npm install @familiar-ai/client
```

## The stores

<Code code={client} lang="ts" title="client.ts" />

There's a store for each stream: `createWorkspaceStore(url, options)` for who the Familiars are, the rooms this person sees and the sign-in; `createFamiliarStore(url, id, options)` for one Familiar's model, memory and schedules; and `createRoomStore(url, id, options)` for one room. Each opens its stream straight away. A store offers every command; one your host's [`allow`](/familiar/build/serve-the-api/#decide-who-may-do-what) refuses rejects with its 403, so render only the UI each person may use. The optional `fetch` makes every request, including stream reconnects, so you can attach a fresh credential each time. An open stream keeps the credentials it started with until it reconnects.

A store's state is plain data from its stream. Read it with `getState()` and `subscribe()`:

- the workspace's `familiars`, `rooms`, `me` and `account`: every room arrives as a sidebar lists it, with its newest entry, what this person hasn't read and whose turns are in progress, so a list needs no stream per room
- a Familiar's `model`, `memory`, `episodes` and `schedules`
- a room's `view` and `history`, its log and the older entries loaded before it; `turns`, its turns in progress; and `transcript`, the derived chat items and whether a Familiar is `busy` here

Change things by calling the commands on the store itself: the workspace's `familiars`, `rooms`, `me`, `account`, `push`, `connections` and `mcp`; a Familiar's `model`, `memory` and `schedules`; a room's `send`, `stop`, `read` and `loadOlder`. They never change identity, so you can pass them around freely. `workspace.familiars.dm(id)` resolves to the room ID of this person's DM with a Familiar, created if new. Call a room's `read(entry)` with the newest entry the person has seen, such as when they open it, to clear its unread count.

Streamed documents are `undefined` until they arrive, and `null` when the server sends none.

`send(text, mentions?)` posts a message with a fresh `requestId`. The host decides who sent it. In a named room, a Familiar mentioned answers, else the room's lead, or each Familiar in turn in a room without one; `composeMessage` builds the text and mentions from what a composer picked, so `@Ada` typed without picking her addresses no one.

## The transcript

`state.transcript.items` is what a chat shows, in order. Each item has an `id` that stays the same across updates. Use it as the key.

- `message`: a person's words, with their `author`, when they were posted and any `mentions`
- `reply`: a Familiar's `text`, `thinking` and `toolCalls`, with which `familiar` and its `name`, `streaming`, `stopped` and any `error`
- `scheduled`: a schedule's prompt arriving, with its `due` time and `creator`
- `waiting`: a Familiar has a turn here with nothing to show yet: `queued` behind work in this room, `elsewhere` while it works in another room, or `running` before its reply starts

While a reply streams, only its current round shows. When the turn ends, the whole reply, every tool call included, replaces it.

Each tool call has a `name`, `arguments`, `status` (`running`, `done` or `error`), text `output` and optional `details`. `details` is whatever the tool returned for UIs. Narrow it before you render it.

Older entries arrive through `room.loadOlder()`. `state.history.status` is `more`, `loading`, `failed` or `start`.

## The connection

`state.connection` moves through these values:

| Value          | Meaning                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `connecting`   | The first stream request is under way                                          |
| `open`         | A compatible protocol handshake has arrived; values follow                     |
| `reconnecting` | A network error, closed stream, 5xx or 429. The store retries with fresh state |
| `unauthorized` | The stream was answered 401 or 403. Retries stop                               |
| `failed`       | Any other unusable answer, such as a 404. Retries stop                         |
| `outdated`     | The protocol handshake was missing or incompatible. Retries stop               |

The store never reloads the page or signs anyone in. After a terminal state, sign-out or an identity change, call `store.disconnect()` and create a new store. Commands reject with the server's error and aren't retried. Commands already sent still settle after you disconnect.

## React

Install React 18 or 19, then use the separate `/react` entry:

<Code code={react} lang="tsx" title="App.tsx" />

Create the store once, outside render, where your app manages connections. `RoomProvider` gives its subtree a room store, and nested providers each give their own. The provider doesn't open or close it. `useRoom` compares selections with `Object.is`, so return stable values such as a single field. `useRoomStore()` returns the nearest provider's store, for its commands. For the workspace's and Familiars' stores, use Zustand's `useStore`. The vanilla entry doesn't load React.
